name: Layered MVC architecture
description: API layer (lua/nit/api/) fetches GitHub data via gh CLI → State layer (lua/nit/state/) centralizes mutable state with observer subscriptions → Controller (lua/nit/controller.lua) orchestrates data loading and refresh → Orchestration layer (lua/nit/orchestration/) manages versioning, snapshots, and mutation queuing → Display layer (lua/nit/display/) renders signs, highlights, popups, and thread panel → Navigation (lua/nit/navigation.lua) handles buffer-level keybindings → Review module (lua/nit/review.lua) manages session lifecycle → Commands (lua/nit/commands.lua) dispatches user commands. Entry point: plugin/nit.lua registers :Nit command. Note: lua/nit/ui/ contains only highlights.lua (highlight group definitions); all rendering lives in lua/nit/display/.

name: Key abstractions
description: Result<T> type: { ok=true, data=... } or { ok=false, error='...' } for all fallible async ops. Parallel operation: api.parallel(operations, callback) in lua/nit/api/parallel.lua — takes array of {fn, args}, returns cancel function, calls callback when all complete. Observer pattern: state.subscribe(key, callback) returns unsubscriber — used by display layer to react to state changes. Request tracker: lua/nit/api/tracker.lua — global registry of cancel functions, cancel_all() stops all in-flight requests. Orchestration abstractions: versioning (per-thread mutation version counter in lua/nit/orchestration/versioning.lua), snapshot (captures and restores thread state for rollback in lua/nit/orchestration/snapshot.lua), queue (per-thread serial mutation queue with 1100ms throttle in lua/nit/orchestration/queue.lua).

name: Data flows
description: Load flow: :Nit start → commands.dispatch() → review.start() sets up background infrastructure (highlights, signs, BufEnter autocmd, state observer) → controller.load() fetches PR (GraphQL) → parallel fetch of files+threads → state subscribers notified → display_manager re-renders per-buffer signs and highlights. Update flow: :Nit refresh → controller.refresh() = cleanup() + load(). File open flow: user opens PR file normally → BufEnter autocmd in review.lua calls try_attach_buffer() → display_manager.attach(bufnr, filepath) applies signs and highlights. State change flow: state mutation → observers.notify() → vim.schedule() batches rapid updates → subscribers callback → display_manager re-renders.

name: Error handling strategy
description: Result type used for all fallible ops — no thrown exceptions in normal flow. API level: pcall() wraps gh CLI invocations, returns Result with error message. Controller level: checks result.ok, calls state.set_error() on failure, cancels related requests. Observer level: pcall() wraps callbacks, logs errors via notification if callback throws. State reset: controller.cleanup() clears error state on new load. Gap: state.set_error() notifies observers but no display code currently subscribes to error state or renders it — error state infrastructure exists but is effectively unused on the display side.

title: Core product design decisions
rationale: Background-only display (no sidebar): workflow-agnostic, doesn't force layout — outcome good. gh CLI over direct REST/GraphQL: handles auth, SSO, token management — outcome good. Observer pattern for state: decouples API fetching from UI updates — outcome good. Ambient by default: nothing demands a new workflow or mandatory UI. Workflow-agnostic entry points: actions reachable from commands or existing buffers, not a dedicated panel. User-initiated surfaces: any UI (popups, menus) appears only when explicitly requested. Lightweight state: minimal review state, avoid persistent systems unless necessary. Lua API only (no keybindings): plugin exposes API, user maps keys.

name: viewer-login-fetch
description: api/viewer.lua calls gh api user --jq .login, trims result; controller.lua fires fetch_viewer in parallel with fetch_pr (independent, cancel tracked); on success calls data.set_viewer_login(); failures silently degrade (no error state set)

name: reaction-normalization
description: normalize_reaction_groups() converts GraphQL reactionGroups (content, viewerHasReacted, reactors.totalCount) to ReactionGroup[] (content, count, viewer_has_reacted). Duplicated inline in comments.lua and mutations.lua per anti-barrel-files convention.
